$comment: Model aliases by intelligence tier, plus the permission reviewer's chain. Aliases cannot target other aliases, so every entry is a concrete model. A tier carries one opencode-go rung, not a stack: the Go quota is shared, so a drained pool fails every Go model at once and a second rung only helps if the first model's own monthly cap binds, which for a cheap model's 250M+ tokens it never does (ADR-0125). Rung order inside a tier is ADR-0103's — lead by capability, then turn completion observed here, then agentic benchmark evidence, then price — and prices, caps and scores are deliberately absent because they move between syncs (ADR-0118): read them from `bin/pi-model-cost`. The rejected alternatives — `gemini-4-argon`, `hy4`, `muse-spark-1.3-contributor`, fable, the Google pair and the free models — sit in `docs/BACKLOG.md` with why each is out and what would promote it. `muse-spark-1.3-contributor` scores above every rung here at a lower drain, but its endpoint trains on request data and it is on trial outside the tiers until that trade is judged — select it directly. A tier spans claude-bridge, opencode-go, openai-codex and the free opencode-go models because those are the separate pools, which is the only availability hedge a rung list can hold — but claude-bridge splits one five-hour window across every tier, so it commits in proportion to how much traffic the earlier tiers already sent (ADR-0125 has the measurements). `glm-5.3` is the Go rung behind `top` and `mid`: `deepseek-v4.1-flash` wins four of the eight weighted evaluations but loses Terminal-Bench 4.0 and CritPt v2 by eight points each, which are the two closest to this agent's work. `cheap` keeps `deepseek-v4.1-flash`, whose turns ask for less, at a tenth of the token price and a lower drain outside peak hours; `top` therefore leads with Opus opportunistically and expects to run glm-5.3, then codex's gpt-5.6-terra when Go's window is spent too; the free models close `cheap` and `mid` after every scored rung (ADR-0120) with one reviewer prompt each as their only evidence, and beam-free takes no images so it stays reviewer-only. `reviewer` is ordered for latency and availability rather than capability: Gemini's free tier and the free Go models answer in 1-2s once the paid quotas are gone, while Haiku averages ~10s of session startup, so firstEventMs stays 30s to cover Haiku's tail and gemini-3.5-flash-lite's 28s. claude-bridge serves the reviewer only through the pi-claude-bridge#216 standalone-prompt patches and refuses a follow-up review's multi-turn conversation either way, hence followUpReviews off. Groq stays out: its free tiers cap at 2-8k TPM against a ~14k-token reviewer prompt.
